chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

And the floating [fish] was mentioned, and what people dislike from it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The floating [fish] that is disliked is from the fish, and it is that whose smell has changed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a floating fish being considered makruh (disliked) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi refutes the common folk belief that all floating fish are makruh, establishing a precise jurisprudential criterion based on olfactory change rather than mere position. By linking the dislike to altered scent, the Imam aligns the ruling with the general principle of impurity (najasah) or spoilage, demonstrating the Shia method of distinguishing between cultural superstition and legal evidence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
, and the floating fish were mentioned and the people dislike from it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, the floating from the fish are abhorred and it is what its smell has changed’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Once, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
mentioned fish which floats on water and what people dislike. He (the Imam) said, ‘The fish floating on the water are disliked because their smell has changed.’”
